title: Safety Signs & Signals Cheat Sheet
summary: Every kind of safety sign by shape and colour, plus the hand and acoustic signals, on two pages.

pages.heading: Safety signs: shape and colour tell you the type

blocks.text: You can tell what a safety sign means from its shape and colour before you read it. Learn the five kinds and the test questions on signs become easy.

blocks.title: The five kinds of safety sign

rows: Red circle and diagonal bar, black pictogram on white
Yellow triangle, black edge and black pictogram
Green rectangle or square, white pictogram
Red rectangle or square, white pictogram
notes: Prohibition: red is at least 35% of the sign. Warning, mandatory, escape and fire signs: the colour is at least 50%.

blocks.title: Rules to remember

items.text: Employers MUST provide and maintain safety signs where a risk can't be avoided or reduced in other ways.

items: Words can be added to a sign, but a fire safety sign with words only isn't acceptable.
Obstacles and drops: yellow and black, or red and white, stripes at about 45°.
Vehicle routes: clearly visible lines, preferably white or yellow.

blocks.title: Quick memory aid
blocks.text: Red circle = don't. Yellow triangle = watch out. Blue circle = do. Green = safe way out or first aid. Red rectangle = fire equipment.

rows: Both arms out horizontally, palms forward
Right arm pointing up, palm forward
Both hands clasped at chest height
Right arm up, palm forward, slowly circling
Right arm down, palm in, slowly circling
Both arms pointing up, palms forward
notes: Hand signals from recognised codes (eg BS 7121 for cranes) may be used instead.

items.text: The signaller MUST be able to see all the manoeuvres without being put in danger.
The signaller's duties MUST be only directing the manoeuvre and keeping nearby workers safe.
An operator who can't carry on safely MUST stop and ask the signaller for new instructions.
The acoustic signal for evacuation MUST be continuous.
